03-03-2026 16-03-2026 The first two weeks of March marked a deliberate gear shift. Capital preservation gave way to high-conviction growth plays after trailing stops did their job on GE, MU, and LMT during that early-month turbulence. The freed-up cash went straight into the "AI Power & Infra" thesis, concentrated in NVDA, ORCL, and NBIS. Defense didn't get abandoned, though. LMT came back into the portfolio alongside ITA to keep the geopolitical hedge intact. On the retail side, WMT wasn't pulling its weight relative to the sector, so it got swapped for TGT after solid earnings data confirmed the thesis. The WMT exit was overdue. The position was dragging behind the broader consumer discretionary space, and TGT (610 units) offered a cleaner entry with better near-term momentum. Simple upgrade in quality, nothing exotic.
The real alpha play was channeling stopped-out capital into NVDA and ORCL right before the GTC Conference window. Timing mattered here. The AI infrastructure narrative had a concrete catalyst on the calendar, and sitting in cash while that played out would have been a waste of the rotation opportunity.
LMT's re-entry deserves its own note. The trailing stop that triggered wasn't a conviction call; it was mechanical. The original macro thesis on rising global military budgets hadn't changed one bit. So the correction was manual: re-enter LMT, add ITA for broader defense diversification, and restore the portfolio's intended structure.		 Learned
Trailing stops worked exactly as designed on GE and MU. They locked in gains during volatility. But the LMT situation exposed a gap: when a stop fires on a position you still believe in fundamentally, you need a re-entry protocol, not just a "wait and see" reflex. That's a process improvement I'm codifying going forward. The Gemini-driven tech selloff also reinforced something I already suspected; high-beta names need wider stop buffers. Tight stops on volatile positions just generate unnecessary churn.
Next Steps
NVDA and ORCL are the immediate watchlist. Post-conference price action will dictate whether stops get tightened or left loose. SIEGY is on the radar as a potential European industrial hedge, worth a deeper look in the next cycle. And IBB's recent leadership in biotech raises a real question: does it merit scaling from a satellite position into a core allocation? That answer depends on whether the momentum sustains through April.
 
17-03-2026 30-03-2026 With 12 trading days remaining and the portfolio sitting last in class rankings, the team invoked the emergency clause in Section 5 of the Team Charter to override the standard 60% equity / moderate-risk mandate. The market entered a confirmed correction: the S&P 500 is down 8.82% YTD, the Nasdaq is in correction territory, and geopolitical escalation (US-Iran, war deadline fears) is driving a broad risk-off environment.

The team executed a full liquidation of underperforming and thesis-broken longs (SPY, TSM, TGT, PG, IONQ, NBIS, JNJ) and redeployed ~$495,000 into an offensive turnaround allocation: PSQ and SH as inverse index hedges to profit directly from the ongoing correction, GLD as a safe-haven capital flight trade, and AA and CENX as a geopolitical momentum trade following Middle East supply disruptions to aluminum markets. Two execution errors (misclicks on TSM and TGT) were identified and corrected immediately within the same session and documented transparently in the log.		 1. Emergency charter override and full liquidation of longs: The thesis for holding SPY, TSM, TGT, PG, IONQ, NBIS and JNJ broke under a confirmed market correction. Holding them was optimising for "hope the market recovers" rather than trading the actual environment. Liquidating freed $495K in capital to deploy offensively.

2. PSQ + SH inverse ETF allocation ($247K combined): The Nasdaq is in correction and the S&P is down ~9%. Buying inverse ETFs converts further market decline into direct positive portfolio returns, he only rational strategy when the trend is unambiguously down with 12 days left.

 3. AA + CENX aluminum trade ($123K combined): A same-day geopolitical news catalyst (Middle East supply disruption) drove aluminum stocks up ~7% in a single session. This is a momentum trade with a clear, short-term, real-world catalyst, the type of trade uniquely suited to a 12-day closing window.		 The most important lesson from this simulation is that strategy must be adaptive, not static. Our original charter was built for a stable market; it was the wrong tool for a correction. Waiting too long to invoke the emergency override cost us several weeks of slow bleed.

Next steps: monitor PSQ and SH daily, if the market shows a confirmed reversal signal (Fed pivot language, peace deal, strong jobs data), exit inverse positions immediately and rotate back into quality longs. Monitor AA and CENX for 3–5 day momentum window and set internal stops at. Final portfolio review scheduled for last trading log.
31-03-2026 11-04-2026 Ceasefire Regime Shift & Adaptive Redeployment. The April 8 ceasefire announcement triggered a full macro regime shift, invalidating the inverse-ETF and war-premium thesis built in the prior period. The team executed an adaptive pivot — closing all eight war-premium positions (PSQ, SH, AA, LMT, XLP, CENX, ITA, MU) and redeploying into a recovery allocation (SPY, ESGU, XLF, XLI, CAT, JPM, XOM, GLD). (1) Exiting PSQ/SH immediately on ceasefire confirmation to eliminate negative beta exposure as markets reversed. (2) Maintaining GLD: the safe-haven thesis evolved — gold's driver shifted from geopolitical fear to dollar weakness and rate-cut expectations, validating the hold. (3) Contrarian XOM top-up: the market over-discounted the Hormuz reopening speed; physical shipping bottlenecks (800+ vessels backlogged) meant the supply normalisation thesis was structurally correct but played out over a longer horizon than the simulation window.  More in depth in the report.

The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis explains April 8, markets repriced the binary geopolitical event faster than fundamental analysis from the team could justify. The Trading Risk overwhelmed conviction-based positioning in the final 48 hours due to noise and simulation maturity nearby.
